modelLimitations.title: Educational model - limitations
items: Research & education only - not a medical device, and not for diagnosis, treatment, or any patient-specific decision.
0D lumped-parameter model: it does not resolve spatial blood flow, local wall stress, or 3D hemodynamics.
Parameters are calibration targets, not fixed physiological constants; outputs are approximate and not yet validated against clinical data.
Several subsystems are not modeled yet (coronary circulation, renal/hepatic/portal beds, detailed baroreflex, fluid exchange).
Use it to build intuition and explore hypotheses - not to predict a specific patient.

normal-reference.title: Normal Physiology Reference
normal-reference.objective: Learn to read the four core panels - waveforms, PV loop, metrics, and controls - at a normal resting operating point, so you have an anchor to compare every disease case against.

acute-anterior-mi.title: Acute Anterior MI: when the pump stalls
acute-anterior-mi.objective: Recognize how an isolated loss of anterior-wall contractility narrows the LV PV loop, drops SV and CO, and raises left atrial pressure.

systolic-heart-failure.title: Systolic Heart Failure (HFrEF)
systolic-heart-failure.objective: Understand how a weak left ventricle lowers stroke volume and cardiac output, raises filling pressure, and reshapes the PV loop.

diastolic-heart-failure.title: Diastolic Heart Failure (HFpEF)
diastolic-heart-failure.objective: Understand how a stiff, poorly relaxing LV raises filling pressures while EF stays normal, and recognize the HFpEF signature on the PV loop, waveforms, and metrics.

aortic-stenosis.title: Aortic Stenosis: a stiff door on the way out
aortic-stenosis.objective: Understand how a narrowed aortic valve forces the left ventricle to generate high pressure, and read that compensation off the PV loop, the LVP-AoP pressure gradient, and the stroke-volume metrics versus a normal heart.

hypovolemic-shock.title: Hypovolemic Shock
hypovolemic-shock.objective: Understand how losing circulating blood volume drops preload, stroke volume, and blood pressure.

normal-sinus.title: Normal physiology
normal-sinus.description: A roughly-physiological resting adult - the reference operating point all other cases deviate from.

acute-anterior-mi.title: Acute Anterior MI: when the pump stalls
acute-anterior-mi.description: A normal heart vs an acute anterior MI heart: an isolated loss of anterior-wall contractility narrows the LV PV loop, drops stroke volume and cardiac output, and raises left atrial filling pressure.

systolic-heart-failure.title: Systolic Heart Failure (HFrEF)
systolic-heart-failure.description: A normal left ventricle compared with a failing one (HFrEF). Reduced contractility plus higher afterload drops stroke volume and cardiac output while raising filling pressure - read it on the waveforms, the PV loop, and the metrics.

diastolic-heart-failure.title: Diastolic Heart Failure (HFpEF)
diastolic-heart-failure.description: A stiff, slow-relaxing left ventricle with preserved ejection fraction, compared with the normal reference. Filling pressures rise even though the pump is intact.

aortic-stenosis.title: Aortic Stenosis: a stiff door on the way out
aortic-stenosis.description: A severely stenotic aortic valve compared with the normal reference: the ventricle builds a large pressure gradient and a tall PV loop to maintain output.

hypovolemic-shock.title: Hypovolemic Shock
hypovolemic-shock.description: A normal heart compared with one that has lost circulating volume: reduced preload narrows and left-shifts the PV loop, dropping stroke volume, cardiac output, and pressure.

lv-failure-dobutamine.title: Cardiogenic shock: LV failure +/- dobutamine
lv-failure-dobutamine.description: Severe global LV pump failure, and the response to a beta-1 inotrope (dobutamine). Compare the two side by side: CO and arterial pressure recover, filling pressure falls.

valve-lesions.title: Valvular lesions: aortic stenosis & mitral regurgitation
valve-lesions.description: Two classic left-heart valve lesions. AS imposes a systolic LV-aortic pressure gradient; MR sends a regurgitant jet into the LA, raising LAP and cutting forward output.

hypovolemia.title: Hypovolemia
hypovolemia.description: Reduced circulating volume (e.g. haemorrhage): preload falls, so stroke volume and cardiac output drop while the heart itself is normal - a preload, not a pump, problem.
